messages:
maya: Heads-up — CI perf job 2026-03-17 shows a ~12% 99th latency regression on small-batch chat workloads after landing PR #4021 (hybrid flash/paged selector).
liam: ugh. does it reproduce locally or only on n1/nightly infra?
sasha: reproduced on my 8xA10 repro with the loadgen (bs=1, seq=512). tail jumps around when we hit branch that uses flash_hybrid_v2 kernel.
maya: attaching quick profiler sample from the canary run:
profiler-bot: ```
Top kernels (aggregated):
  flash_hybrid_v2_kernel         72.3%
  paged_attention_kernel        17.8%
  kv_memcpy_and_pad_overhead     6.4%
  dtype_casts_and_sync           3.5%
KV cache layout: interleaved, bf16 pinned. Batch shape distribution: 85% bs=1, 10% bs=2, 5% bs=4.
```
devon: interesting that kv_memcpy shows up — were we hitting extra copies when switching kernels?
liam: probably. hybrid selector currently switches kernel at runtime and does an on-the-fly layout conversion for interleaved->paged-friendly view. that copy is O(seq*hidden) and we didn't account for the bs=1-heavy tail.
sasha: repro snippet I used: ``./badger --model redwood-small --batching=auto --seq=512 --drivers=flash_hybrid_v2,paged``
liam: can you dump the timeline (cudaMemcpy, kernel launches)?
sasha: pasted a short flame excerpt: ``Memcpy H2D 4.2ms -> launch flash_hybrid_v2 0.8ms -> memcpy D2D (layout transpose) 3.9ms -> launch paged 1.1ms``
maya: so the selector falls back mid-request and triggers a D2D transpose that kills tail. Any ideas for mitigations?
devon: a few options: 1) avoid runtime layout conversion by requiring kernel-compatible layout up-front (pin flash_hybrid_v1 for now), 2) cache converted KV pages per-request (memory tradeoff), 3) change batcher to prefer kernels that match current cache layout for bs=1 heavy workloads.
liam: +1 to 3 — batching heuristics could bias routing so we don't flip kernels for tiny batches. We already have a scoring function; we can add kv_layout_mismatch_penalty.
sasha: I prototyped a simple heuristic: if bs==1 and seq>256, add 50ms penalty to any path that requires kv-transpose. early results: tail reduces by ~9% in lab.
maya: that sounds promising. Can we avoid the D2D copy entirely by performing layout-agnostic kernel path? e.g., support both interleaved and separate views in the kernel and pick codepath without copy?
devon: possible but increases kernel complexity and register pressure. flash_hybrid_v2 was already tuned for bf16 interleaved. adding both paths probably regresses throughput.
liam: for immediate relief let's roll back the hybrid selector to always prefer flash_v1 on small instances and land the kv_layout_mismatch_penalty change. I'll open a rollback/canary plan.
maya: please also add a regression test in perf-bench for bs=1 seq=512 targeting 99th latency.
liam: opening PR now — will pin canary to 10% of traffic for 30m, monitor tail. (PR: #4042)
deploy-bot: canary started: 10% traffic on us-west-2-small at 2026-03-17T16:12:00Z :rocket:
profiler-bot: quick canary snapshot after 10m: flash_hybrid_v2 usage dropped 82% on canary, kv_memcpy overhead down to 1.1%.
sasha: nice. once canary is stable we should design a longer-term plan: either change KV cache layout to make both kernels happy (separate banks + alignment hints) or refactor kernel-selection to avoid copies.
maya: agreed — add to roadmap: "kv-layout compatibility strategy" and schedule a 2-hour design session this week. assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml. :calendar:
liam: thanks all. I'll post the PR and follow-up notes in the repo. :eyes:
